title: Retro 32-Bit Low-Poly Horror Scene
summary: An atmospheric late-90s console style horror frame: low polygon geometry, warped unfiltered textures, heavy distance fog, dithered colour and a 320x240 look, with a single light source and an unsettling hint of a threat. Slots for location, light source and threat.
prompt:
A single in-game frame from a low-poly survival horror game rendered to look exactly like a late-1990s home console title, output as if captured at 320x240 and upscaled with nearest-neighbour pixels.

Location: {argument name="location" default="a narrow corridor in an abandoned roadside motel at night, doors on both sides, one door ajar"}.
Light source: {argument name="light_source" default="the player character flashlight, a hard cone of yellowish light"}.
Threat: {argument name="threat" default="a tall, thin silhouette standing motionless at the far end of the corridor, barely visible in the fog"}.

# Retro 3D rendering rules
- Very low polygon counts: visibly faceted walls, door frames and props; characters built from a few hundred triangles.
- Low-resolution textures around 64x64, unfiltered (no bilinear smoothing), with affine texture warping visible on large floor and wall polygons.
- Slight vertex jitter look: edges not perfectly straight, small gaps where polygons meet.
- Thick distance fog fading geometry to {argument name="fog_colour" default="murky dark green-grey"} within a short draw distance.
- 15-bit colour with visible ordered dithering in the gradients; no smooth modern gradients.

# Composition and camera
- Fixed, slightly high camera angle looking down the corridor, as in classic fixed-camera horror games, with the player character visible from behind in the lower third.
- The flashlight cone is the brightest area; the threat sits just at the edge of the light, readable only as a silhouette.
- Lots of negative space and darkness; one red or warm accent ({argument name="accent" default="a flickering exit sign"}) to draw the eye.

# Mood
Quiet dread, not gore. Lonely, humid, wrong.

# Avoid
Modern PBR materials, high-resolution textures, ray-traced reflections, depth of field, film-grain noise instead of dithering, blood or gore, UI, text, watermarks, any recognisable existing game character or monster.
